conclusion: Adding the paper title and section to each passage before embedding gave the best ranking (MRR 0.31 → 0.41, hit@1 0.20 → 0.30) at no runtime cost. Off-the-shelf rerankers found more answers within the top 10 but ranked them lower, and were 2–20× slower. With 10 answerable questions, these are indicative results.

experiments.name: baseline
experiments.takeaway: Reference row: evidence in the top 6 for 4 of 10 questions; Q2 (bert-01) and Q4 (lora-01) rank 12 and 19, and no row finds rag-02's evidence within 20.

experiments.name: rerank-minilm-l6
experiments.takeaway: Pulls 9 of 10 into the top 10 (baseline 5) but seldom to the top: hit@6 +1 question, MRR falls to 0.246, and it is 20 times slower (3.9 s a question).

experiments.name: rerank-tinybert
experiments.takeaway: Same hit@6 as MiniLM (+1 question) at an eighth of its time (0.46 s), but MRR falls to 0.260 and only 7 of 10 reach the top 10.

experiments.name: hybrid-rrf60
experiments.takeaway: Best hit@6 (0.6, +2 questions) at no extra cost: keywords lift the RAG and Transformer questions, though MRR stays level (0.315) and Q2 drops to 17.

experiments.name: prefix
experiments.takeaway: Best MRR (0.407) and hit@1 (0.3), +1 question at hit@6 and 9 of 10 in the top 10, including Q2 at 7; it needs the library re-embedded.

experiments.name: prefix-hybrid
experiments.takeaway: The two ideas add up: the best hit@6 (0.7) and MRR (0.425) of any row at 0.15 s a question, though hit@1 is 0.2 (prefix alone 0.3) and Q2 still ranks 14.
